thread:
jamie: quick heads-up — ran a microprofiler against host parse/tokenize on a 4k token workload, and we have a consistent ~18-22% CPU overhead compared to the kernel-batched path :thinking:
jamie: attached top lines from the flame (trimmed):
```
host_parse(): 42%
  tokenize(): 27%
    utf8_normalize(): 9%
  http2_frame_decode(): 8%
  kv_cache_lookup(): 5%
grpc_writev_shim(): 3%
```
jamie: this is on the grpc path with continuous-streaming enabled — not the HTTP/1 fast path. looks like tokenize + http2 framing + small kv hits are the culprits.
sasha: ugh. did you run with kernel-selection pinned to the fast-attn variant? or the fallback quant path?
jamie: pinned to fast-attn (v2) for the model. kernel selection seems fine on GPU side — this is host-side CPU. suspecting fragmentation from framing + repeated utf8 work.
ben: can you paste the stdlib tracer output? curious about allocations and memcpy hotspots.
jamie: here, quick trace snippet:
```
ALLOC  12.3MB  host_preparse::buffer_grow
MEMCPY 4.1MB  http2_frame_decode -> tokenize
LOCK   0.8ms  kv_cache::shard_mutex  (hot shard 3)
```
jamie: kv shard mutex spikes align with some of the tail latencies.
olga: how warm is KV cache during the run? are we getting cross-request prefix reuse?
jamie: warm but low reuse for these synthetic streams — most requests are unique prompt prefixes. cache hit rate ~22%.
mike: low reuse + high mutex cost rings bad. maybe try sharded per-CPU LRU and relax locks (R/W)?
ben: also consider pre-normalizing UTF-8 once at ingress and keep a view into buffer rather than memcpy between framing and tokenize.
sasha: +1. we also saw grpc_writev_shim() cause 2-3% overhead when chunk sizes are <512B. continuous-streaming currently flushes too eagerly.
jamie: good point — here's a small repro I used (pseudocode):
```
for req in stream:
  send(req.prefix)
  send(req.piece1)
  send(req.piece2)
  end
```
jamie: many tiny writes => grpc framing + writev drain.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment 2026-03-23T12:25:00Z: canary/host-parse-opt started (2 pods)
ben: experiment idea: add a framing coalescer that merges writes within 1ms or up to 2KB. should reduce writev syscalls and http2 frame overhead.
olga: implementable as a sidecar buffer or in-host preparse layer. sidecar easier but adds hop.
mike: sidecar adds latency though. can we do coalescing in the ingress thread with async flush? that keeps single hop.
jamie: ran a quick patch: coalesce 1ms/2KB on ingress thread + UTF8 pre-normalize. rough results: tail p99 latency dropped 15%, CPU for tokenize down ~10%, overall host CPU down 12%.
sasha: nice. did that change affect batching heuristics on GPU? we rely on small inter-arrival spacing to trigger minibatching.
jamie: slight effect — batch sizes decreased by 0.5 tokens average in this synthetic test (we delayed micro-writes), but overall GPU throughput unchanged; the latency win dominated.
ben: what about KV cache behavior? coalescing might increase contiguous prefix lengths and improve hit rate.
jamie: exactly — hit rate moved 22% -> 31% in that run. kv mutex contention reduced noticeably.
olga: any regression on HTTP/1 path? we don't want to degrade normal API customers.
jamie: HTTP/1 path unaffected (we gated coalescing only on streaming/grpc small-write scenarios). toggled by header X-Stream-Coalesce.
mike: we should still add a low-overhead kernel that precomputes UTF8 normalization table for common codepoints. avoids per-byte scans.
ben: +1. also consider a lightweight zero-copy token view that'll let GPU path access buffer slices without memcpy, maybe a shared mmap'ed ring.
sasha: alignment with kernel selection: if host reduces CPU overhead, we can enable the more aggressive kernel (fast-attn) more broadly. measured cost reduction matters for decision trees.
jamie: next steps I propose: 1) land coalescer behind header flag + metrics, 2) add UTF8 pre-normalize in ingress (opt-in), 3) prototype per-CPU KV shards with try_lock fallback, 4) run e2e canary against small-write-heavy traffic.
ben: can you open a perf/regression PR with the microbench harness? tag me and @sasha for review.
jamie: will do. PR coming in ~30m. I'll include the profiler flame + tracer outputs + canary logs.
olga: don't forget to add metric for kv_mutex_wait_ms and grpc_writev_syscalls/s.
mike: adding pointers: we also have existing kernel-selection telemetry (model.kernel_decisions) — let's correlate host_cpu% vs chosen kernel over the canary window.
jamie: good call. I'll add a dashboard panel for that.
sasha: thanks team. excited to see if we can shave another 10-15% host cost. :rocket:
jamie: quick note — if anyone wants to reproduce locally, I put the mini-repro script in my sandbox gist: https://gist.github.com/jamie/host-coalesce-repro (use grpc streaming with small frames)
ben: grabbing it now.
jamie: will follow up with PR link and timeline once canary is green.
